transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account. we also have Diego, our SE, and Priya from partnerships. quick round robin?
00:08 Lena Park: Hi, Lena here from AuroraGrid partnerships, thanks for setting this up. Vikram, Sara, Omar are on as well.
00:15 Diego Alvarez: Great to meet you all. quick agenda: intro, partnership models, technical constraints, security, next steps. sound good?
00:22 Vikram Rao: Yep sounds good. We run a managed GPU marketplace, we resell capacity and also offer co-lo racks in our hubs. we're interested in Redwood for both a native integration and a managed offering.
00:40 Maya Chen: Awesome. high level, Redwood offers hosted API, dedicated capacity, and private deployments. for partners we usually look at one of three patterns: reseller (we ship models on your infra), deep integration (API routing to AuroraGrid), or co-marketed dedicated clusters.
00:58 Sara Kim: Quick question: when you say private deployment, is that full customer-managed VPC with a control plane you don't touch, or do you host a control plane in your environment?
01:12 Diego Alvarez: Good Q. we have a few options: private control plane where the customer owns the network and keys (typical for regulated customers), or a hybrid where control plane is in Redwood but we peer into customer VPC for data plane. there are tradeoffs around metrics and autoscaling.
01:33 Omar Haddad: From security perspective we need to confirm KMS integration and whether model cache or logs ever persist outside customer-controlled storage.
01:42 Maya Chen: Totally. we support customer-managed KMS, and audit logs can be exported to your SIEM. KV cache is configurable — for most private installs it's in customer-owned ephemeral storage. we'll share the security crib sheet.
01:55 Lena Park: Great. can you talk through latency/cost tradeoffs? our customers often ask about per-token cost vs p99 latency, especially for chat workloads.
02:08 Diego Alvarez: Sure. latency is mostly a function of instance type and batching. if you go with dedicated capacity on AuroraGrid GPUs, we can maintain low p99 by tuning batching window and using our runtime optimizations. cost depends on utilization; prefix caching and batching reduce tokens served. note: if network hop to a hosted Redwood control plane exists, add 10-30ms depending on region.
02:33 Vikram Rao: Our H100 nodes are in eu-west-1 and us-west-2. network is good, but depending on peering there may be egress hops. we can do direct peering.
02:45 Diego Alvarez: Perfect. direct peering avoids the extra hop. we should capture your ASN and nearest PoP for the benchmark.
02:55 Sara Kim: what's a typical pilot look like? how long, who pays for infra?
03:02 Maya Chen: we usually do a 4–12 week pilot. common approach: Redwood runs a benchmark on partner infra using a limited dataset, we measure throughput/latency and validate model outputs. sometimes partner covers infra for the first run; other times we do a co-funded trial. we'll propose terms.
03:20 Vikram Rao: ok, we can carve out 4 H100s for a week for the benchmark. need to confirm network and credentials.
03:29 Diego Alvarez: That's ideal. i'll coordinate the benchmark plan and the exact test harness.
03:36 Lena Park: On the commercial side, we're evaluating a reseller revenue share vs fixed monthly retainer for reserved pools. does Redwood have standard partner agreements?
03:46 Priya Nair: Yes, we have a partner program. Typically revenue share for marketplace listings, and for Dedicated we do committed capacity with discounting. we'll share the partner packet after this call.
03:58 Omar Haddad: Back to security, how do you handle data retention for prompts and outputs? customers in finance need guaranteed zero retention or customer-controlled retention.
04:09 Diego Alvarez: In hosted mode we have retention defaults, but enterprise/private deployments can enforce zero retention and customer-managed storage for logs. we can also disable analytics that send token-level info to Redwood.
04:24 Vikram Rao: Good. for PCI-like customers we need explicit attestations. can you provide SOC2 docs and encryption details?
04:33 Maya Chen: Absolutely — we'll attach our SOC2 Type II, ISO summary, and encryption/KMS integration notes.
04:41 Lena Park: any competitors we should be aware of? we've seen interest in Lambda Labs and Paperspace for similar integrations. how do you differentiate?
04:52 Maya Chen: two big differentiators: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private so you don't re-implement clients, and tuning tooling — batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization recommendations — that reduce unit economics. we also emphasize observability for per-route costs.
05:10 Sara Kim: For the integration, what networking options do you need? VPC peering, transit gateway, or private link?
05:20 Diego Alvarez: We support VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink. for cross-region we sometimes recommend a transit gateway or colocated PoP. we'll need a list of allowed CIDRs and NAT/egress rules for the benchmark.
05:34 Vikram Rao: We'll prepare that.
05:36 Lena Park: On the SE side, Diego, will you own the bench plan?
05:39 Diego Alvarez: Yes. next step: i'll share the benchmark plan with test vectors, expected load profiles, and the harness. we'll need SSH or API creds and a small sample dataset.
05:50 Maya Chen: i'll send partnership packet and a starter network diagram, and Priya will follow with commercial options.
05:57 Omar Haddad: timeline question: how long from pilot to GA integration?
06:02 Maya Chen: depends on pilot outcomes, but typical is 8–12 weeks from pilot start to a soft launch for marketplace listings. dedicated/private deployments may take longer based on compliance checks.
06:15 Vikram Rao: One more technical note: some of our customers want model pinning and controlled rollout. does Redwood support rollouts and canarying?
06:25 Diego Alvarez: Yes — we have rollouts, canary, A/B, and automatic fallback policies to compatible model variants if a node fails. we can also pin model versions per-customer.
06:36 Sara Kim: any known gotchas with NVLink topology or multi-GPU jobs on the Redwood runtime?
06:42 Diego Alvarez: For multi-GPU context, we support sharded tensor execution but performance depends on the model and sequence lengths. NVLink is helpful; we recommend testing on your exact instance flavors.
06:56 Lena Park: Sounds good. Omar and Vikram will compile the security and infra docs and we'll aim to have them to you in a few days.
07:05 Maya Chen: Great. recap: Maya sends partner packet + network diagram; Diego sends benchmark plan; AuroraGrid sends infra topology and SOC2 excerpts; Priya sends partner commercial packet.
07:18 Lena Park: Perfect. thanks all.
07:21 Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with artifacts and a proposed pilot SOW. bye.
07:28 [call ends]
